title: Flash-Loan Balance Snapshot
summary: An airdrop rewards holders proportionally to their LIVE token balance. An attacker flash-borrows a fortune for one transaction, claims rewards against the borrowed balance, and repays — all atomically, for free.
web2Analog: Trusting an instantaneous, attacker-inflatable metric (a spot snapshot) for a privileged decision, instead of a value the attacker cannot transiently manufacture.

identify.question: Why can the airdrop rewards be farmed for free?
options: flashLoan() checks that the loan is repaid
claim() snapshots the reward from a live token.balanceOf, so a flash-borrowed balance counts
the claimed mapping prevents claiming twice
identify.explanation: claim() mints rewards equal to token.balanceOf(msg.sender) at call time — an instantaneous spot balance. A flash loan lets the attacker hold a huge balance for the duration of one call, claim against it, and repay in the same transaction.

hints: What balance does claim() use to size the reward — and when is it measured?
A flash loan gives you a massive balance for exactly one transaction. What can you do while holding it?
Inside onFlashLoan(), call airdrop.claim() before repaying the loan.

fix.recommendedFix: Never base entitlements on a live, transiently-inflatable balance. Use a checkpointed balance captured at a fixed snapshot block (e.g. ERC20Votes/ERC20Snapshot), or accrue rewards over time held rather than instantaneous holdings. A flash loan can give any address an arbitrary balance for one transaction, so spot balanceOf must never gate value.
